bio.name: Ruyuan Wan
bio.about:
I am a third-year Ph.D. student in Information Science and Technology at Pennsylvania State University, working with Dr. Ting-hao 'Kenneth' Huang. I am also an NSF Research Traineeship Fellow in the LinDiv: Linguistic Diversity across the Lifespan program. Along the way, I have interned at Apple, IBM Research, Samsung Research America, and Tencent. My work has received two CHI Best Paper Honorable Mention Awards (CHI 2025 and CHI 2026).

Before my Ph.D., I trained across statistics, data science, computer science, and linguistics. I earned a Bachelor's in Statistics and Master's degrees in Data Science and Linguistics at the University of Minnesota, where I was advised by Dr. Lana Yarosh and Dr. Dongyeop Kang. I also earned a Master's in Computer Science at the University of Notre Dame, in the ND-HCI lab.
bio.bio: My research lies at the intersection of Human Computer Interaction (HCI), Natural Language Processing (NLP), and Social Computing. I study how human communication and AI systems co-evolve under algorithmic and interface constraints in complex social contexts. I develop taxonomies, multilingual datasets, and evaluation frameworks that combine LLM benchmarking with qualitative methods, to improve the robustness, fairness, and safety of real-world human-AI systems.
